name: Barcelona 2024-25 (Hansi Flick era, 2024-26)
scopeNote: Id and name keep 24/25 per the user, but the research covers Flick's whole Barcelona era: first competitive match Valencia 1-2 Barcelona, La Liga matchday 1, 17 August 2024 (fcbarcelona.com match report; Flick took charge 1 July 2024), to the latest verifiable competitive match, the El Clasico at Camp Nou on 25 October 2026 (Real Madrid 2-1, single tier C source: Depor; the Depor lineups contain oddities such as 'Xavi Espart', so treat the 2026/27 details with caution). Every source carries its season in eventDate (2024/25, 2025/26, 2026/27). Best documented: 2024/25 (Coaches' Voice, UEFA technical observers, Ara, Soccerway, Cubarsi quotes) and the autumn of 2025/26 (Opta Analyst, Fussball Coaches Newsletter, Total Football Analysis, Sempre Barca on the high-line crisis). 2026/27 is thin (Ara, Al Jazeera, Football Espana, Depor). A narrowing to 2024/25 is possible by filtering eventDate. Style terms used by sources: very high defensive line with offside trap, counter-press, vertical transitions ('more direct towards goal'); the old tiki-taka label is only partly right (Coaches' Voice: fewest long passes in La Liga yet most through balls; Soccerway: Barcelona accept giving Bayern the ball to be more vertical). Marking: UEFA technical observers state Barcelona's back four used a zonal marking system in open play against Bayern (Oct 2024); no source read states the corner-marking system (zonal, man or mixed), so that is open. Season outcomes: 2024/25 domestic treble (La Liga, Copa, Supercopa; Champions League semi-final loss to Inter); 2025/26 La Liga champions (fcbarcelona.es 'Los 10 datos del campeon de Liga', 2026-05-26).
openQuestions: Corner marking (zonal, man-to-man or mixed) is not stated in any page read; needs a set-piece-specific analysis.

El Gol Digital (tier C) reports players questioned the high line after the Copa del Rey semi-final at Atletico (reported 2026-02-14); no official player statement confirms it, and the report is single-source.
2026/27 evidence is thin and the Depor El Clasico report (25 Oct 2026, 1-2 loss) is a single tier C source with odd lineup names; verify against a second source.
Press label 'tiki-taka' versus Flick's own wish to be 'more direct towards goal' (July 2024): possession stayed high (66.5% after 22 games, 68.91% over 2025/26) while through balls led the league.
The Ara 2026-09-10 article says 'tres temporadas de Flick'; consistent with 2024-26 but the 2026/27 Champions League stats should be checked against UEFA.
Average squad age for 2025/26 and 2026/27 and La Masia debut counts per season were not found; only 2024/25 (second-youngest in La Liga; XI average 24.5 vs Bayern in Oct 2024).

statedView.quote: We can (play a) low block and defend in the final third, or we go on our way, our philosophy, how we want to do it, and make things much better
We are Barca, and we play with our DNA. I won't change our style out of fear of losing. I'm not going to sit back and defend a 1-0 lead.
Es clave ser más directos hacía el gol.
Of course our style of play involves risks, but I love it.
If the distances are too big, you’ve lost because you have to run more and you give more time to the opponent and that kills you defensively. That is something we have to change.
La disciplina es necesaria. Me gusta conectar con los jugadores, es crucial. Quiero que me pregunten cosas, tienen mi puerta abierta.
Gerard Lopez (ex-Barca): It's one thing to push forward and do it well ... and another to be... suicidal (criticism of Flick, press label)
